title: Submodular Maximization under Supermodular Constraint: Greedy Guarantees

problem.claim: Maximize a submodular function subject to an upper-bound constraint on a supermodular cost function.

gap.claim: Guarantees for greedy methods and other efficient algorithmic paradigms under supermodular constraints are largely open.

contributions.claim: The paper studies a greedy algorithm that iteratively includes elements maximizing the ratio of the objective and constraint functions.
The greedy algorithm achieves a (1 − e−(1−?))-approximation before stopping, and this approximation is tight for the algorithm.

For objectives with submodular curvature c, the approximation bound improves, and continuing to violate the constraint can improve it further; Greedy-Ratio-Marginal with binary search yields a bicriteria approximation for the dual problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In simulations of LLM agents debating over multiple rounds, the algorithm outperforms all other greedy heuristics.
On smaller simulated problems, the algorithm achieves the same performance as the optimal set found by exhaustive search.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper considers submodular maximization with supermodular cost constraints motivated by data mining and machine learning applications.
The supermodular constraint regime lacks strong, well-understood guarantees for greedy and other efficient methods.
The paper studies upper-bound supermodular cost constraints using a less restrictive curvature notion.
The greedy method receives an approximation guarantee that is reported as tight, with improved bounds under objective curvature and a bicriteria result for the dual problem.
Experiments on simulated multi-round LLM-agent debates report superiority over other greedy heuristics and optimal performance on smaller instances.

source_observation.claim: A ratio-based greedy rule is reported to outperform other greedy heuristics in the described LLM-agent subset-selection simulation.

interpretation.claim: When objective gain and constraint cost can be compared incrementally, a gain-to-cost ratio may provide a useful selection heuristic.

application.claim: Use ratio-based greedy selection as a candidate baseline for subset selection problems with submodular objectives and supermodular costs.

exception.claim: The reported empirical comparison concerns a specific simulation of LLM agents debating over multiple rounds and does not establish performance in other settings.

unknowns: The numerical value or precise definition of the supermodular curvature parameter is not available in the supplied units.
The experimental setup, datasets, baselines, and quantitative results are not specified.
The abstract does not provide the conditions under which the approximation guarantees hold in full detail.
